text: You can catch sickle cell disease by touching or sharing food with a warrior.
explain: Sickle cell is genetic. It is inherited from parents, never spread by contact.

text: Two parents with genotype AS have a 25% chance of a child with SS in each pregnancy.
explain: Each pregnancy carries a 25% chance of SS, 50% of AS, and 25% of AA.

text: Warriors often exaggerate crisis pain to get attention.
explain: Crisis pain is real and can be severe. Disbelief is one of the biggest struggles warriors face.

text: A fever in a person with sickle cell disease is an emergency.
explain: Infections can become serious quickly. A fever needs urgent medical attention.

text: Staying hydrated can help reduce the risk of a crisis.
explain: Dehydration is a common trigger, so drinking enough water matters every day.

text: Sickle cell disease is caused by a curse or witchcraft.
explain: It is caused by a gene change passed from parents to children. Nobody is cursed and nobody is to blame.

text: People with sickle cell disease cannot go to school or hold a job.
explain: With good care and understanding from others, many warriors study, work and achieve great things. They may need rest and water breaks and some time off during a crisis.

text: Prayer or herbal mixtures alone can cure sickle cell disease.
explain: Faith can be a real source of strength, but it does not replace medical care. A bone marrow or stem cell transplant is the established cure, and it is not available to everyone. Regular treatment helps prevent complications.

text: A person with sickle cell disease can look completely healthy and still be in severe pain.
explain: Pain is often invisible. Believing a warrior who says they are in pain is one of the kindest things you can do.

text: A person with genotype AS has sickle cell disease.
explain: AS is a carrier, also called sickle cell trait. Carriers usually stay well but can pass the sickle gene to their children.

text: If one parent is AA and the other is SS, every child will be AS.
explain: Each child receives one normal gene (A) and one sickle gene (S), so every child is a carrier and none have the disease.

text: If two AS parents already have a healthy AA child, their next child cannot have SS.
explain: The chances are the same in every pregnancy. A previous child does not change them.

text: Knowing your genotype before marriage helps couples make informed choices.
explain: A simple blood test gives the answer, and genetic counselling can explain what it means.

text: People with genotype AS usually have crises as severe as people with SS.
explain: Carriers usually stay well. Sickle cell disease, such as SS or SC, is what causes regular crises.

text: Chest pain or trouble breathing in a person with sickle cell disease needs urgent hospital care.
explain: These can be signs of a serious complication. Go to a hospital straight away.

text: Pain medicine at home is always enough, so a hospital visit is never needed.
explain: Severe pain that medicine at home does not ease, or pain with other warning signs, needs a hospital.

text: Sudden weakness on one side of the body or trouble speaking in a warrior needs urgent medical help.
explain: These can be signs of a stroke, which is an emergency. Get to a hospital immediately.

text: Many warriors can enjoy light activity if they drink water and rest when tired.
explain: Heavy exertion, overheating and dehydration can trigger a crisis, but gentle activity with water and rest is often fine. A doctor can advise each person.

text: Cold weather and harmattan dryness can trigger a crisis.
explain: Cold and dry air are common triggers. Keep warm, drink more water and moisturise during harmattan.

text: Taking prescribed medicines and attending clinic regularly helps prevent complications.
explain: Regular care helps keep warriors healthier and can reduce hospital visits.

text: Living with sickle cell can affect a person's mood, and talking to someone helps.
explain: Long-term illness and pain can be exhausting. Supportive friends, family and counsellors make a real difference.
